⭐ 1/5 rating
Bangladesh's Binance P2P market lacks a crucial feature: the ability to distinguish between Personal and Agent Mobile Financial Service (MFS) accounts such as bKash, Nagad, and Rocket.

Due to the absence of proper filtering options, a significant number of orders are canceled every day because buyers and sellers have different account-type requirements. This results in wasted time, reduced trading efficiency, unnecessary disputes, and a poor user experience for both traders and merchants.

Binance has successfully adapted P2P features to meet the needs of local markets in many countries. However, the Bangladesh P2P market still lacks a basic and highly requested functionality that directly impacts daily trading activities.

We urgently request the implementation of:

• Personal Account Filter
• Agent Account Filter
• Custom Payment Method Tags
• Mandatory Account Type Display Before Order Creation

Addressing this issue would significantly improve transparency, reduce order cancellations, enhance user satisfaction, and create a more efficient trading environment for the entire Bangladesh P2P community.

We hope Binance will prioritize this long-standing issue and provide a solution as soon as possible.

As verified P2P Merchants from Bangladesh, we fully support Binance's continuous efforts to maintain a zero-tolerance policy against any extra or hidden charges. Transparent pricing creates a secure environment and protects long-term user trust.

Following the strict implementation of this policy, the entire Mobile Financial Services (MFS) P2P market (such as bKash, Nagad, Rocket, and Upay) is facing a technical and structural challenge. In Bangladesh, MFS platforms operate under two completely different account systems: Personal Accounts and Agent Accounts.

Currently, grouping both systems under a single payment tag is causing operational conflicts for both types of merchants and creating confusion for general buyers. To ensure a balanced, fair, and healthy ecosystem for everyone, our entire merchant community collectively proposes the following update:

Separation of MFS Payment Methods: "Personal" and "Agent"

The Problem: Personal and Agent accounts have completely different on daily transaction limits, cash-flow regulations, and operating mechanisms. However, because both account types are merged under a single unified MFS tag (e.g., "bKash", "Nagad", "Rocket", or "Upay"), buyers cannot distinguish between them on the ad list. This often leads to accidental orders, frequent cancellation requests, customer dissatisfaction, and unnecessary trade disputes, as buyers place orders without realizing the specific account requirements. This structural gap creates operational delays for both Personal and Agent merchants.

Our Proposal: We request Binance to split the primary MFS options into distinct payment methods based on account types: for example,

"bKash Personal" / "bKash Agent"
"Nagad Personal" / "Nagad Agent"
"Rocket Personal" / "Rocket Agent"
"Upay Personal" / "Upay Agent".

This structural clarity will allow buyers to filter and trade according to their exact preference, significantly reducing order cancellations and helping both merchant models operate smoothly within their respective spaces without any conflict.

We believe this change would improve transparency, reduce avoidable disputes and order cancellations, enhance user experience, and support Binance's objective of maintaining a fair, efficient, and compliant P2P marketplace in Bangladesh.

Submitted on behalf of the Bangladesh P2P Merchant Community.
